class.name: IcyHttpStream
class.brief_description: Handles HTTP requests and continuous audio streaming from Icecast servers.
class.description: [IcyHttpStream] establishes HTTP connections to Icecast-compatible servers and continuously downloads streaming audio data on a dedicated thread. After the response headers are received, the stream creates an [IcyAudioDecoder] for the [code]Content-Type[/code] header (see [method IcyAudioDecoder.create_for_mime_type]), sets the bitrate from the [code]icy-br[/code] header on it, and sends all downloaded data to it. Get the decoder with [method get_audio_decoder] in the [signal connection_opened] handler. If no decoder is registered for the content type, the connection is closed with [constant RESULT_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT]. If a decoder was set with [method set_audio_decoder], that one is used instead. SHOUTcast v1 servers answer with an [code]ICY 200 OK[/code] line instead of an HTTP status line. These are accepted, and the ICY status code is returned by [method get_response_code] like an HTTP code. The class can also parse ICY metadata embedded in the stream, and emits signals for connection changes and metadata. [IcyRadioPlayer] combines this class with a player node for the common case.

signal.name: connection_opened
signal.description: Emitted when the connection to the server is open and data starts to arrive. The decoder for this connection already exists at this point ([method get_audio_decoder]). Connect to its signals here.

signal.name: connection_closed
signal.description: Emitted when the connection is closed, either intentionally or due to an error. [param result] contains a [enum Result] value describing the reason the connection was closed. [b]Note:[/b] This can fire before [signal connection_opened] (e.g. [constant RESULT_CANT_CONNECT] or a non-2xx status), so handlers must not assume a decoder has been created yet.

signal.name: metadata_received
signal.description: Emitted when ICY metadata is received from the server. The format and contents of [param metadata] depend on the metadata provided by the stream (typically [code]StreamTitle='Artist - Title';[/code]).

method.name: request
method.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to [param url] and attempts to establish a streaming connection. If the connection succeeds, the stream begins downloading data continuously on a dedicated thread until the connection is closed or interrupted. Returns [constant OK] if the request was started, [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if [param url] is malformed (missing or unsupported scheme; only [code]http://[/code] and [code]https://[/code] are accepted), or [constant ERR_BUSY] if a request is already active. Connection failures that happen after this call returns are reported asynchronously through [signal connection_closed]. [param url] specifies the URL of the Icecast stream. [param connect_timeout] is how many seconds the stream waits for the response headers before it gives up with [constant RESULT_TIMEOUT]. This covers name resolution, connecting, the TLS handshake, the request and any redirects. [code]0[/code] disables it. After the headers are received, [member stall_timeout] is used instead. If [param parse_metadata] is [code]true[/code], ICY metadata embedded in the stream is parsed and exposed through the appropriate signals. [param custom_headers] specifies additional HTTP headers to include in the request such as user agent or bearer token. Each entry must be formatted as [code]"Header-Name: Value"[/code].

method.name: cancel_request
method.description: Cancels the active request or stream, if one exists. Blocks until the worker thread has stopped, then emits [signal connection_closed] with [constant RESULT_CANCELLED] (unless a result was already emitted).

method.name: is_requesting
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a request is currently active or data is being streamed. Becomes [code]false[/code] again once the stream ends for any reason, so [method request] can be called again without an explicit [method cancel_request].

method.name: get_content_mime_type
method.description: Returns the MIME type of the streamed media. (e.g [code]"audio/mpeg"[/code] for MP3 streams)

method.name: get_response_code
method.description: Returns the HTTP status code of the last response, or [code]0[/code] if no response has been received yet. Useful for telling apart failures reported as [constant RESULT_REQUEST_FAILED] (e.g. [code]404[/code], [code]403[/code], [code]503[/code]).

method.name: get_audio_decoder
method.description: Returns the decoder that receives the data of the current connection: either the one the stream created for the content type, or the one set with [method set_audio_decoder]. Available from the [signal connection_opened] handler on. [code]null[/code] before the first connection is open.

method.name: get_response_headers
method.description: Returns the raw HTTP response headers.

method.name: get_response_headers_as_dictionary
method.description: Returns the HTTP response headers as a key-value [Dictionary]. Header names are case-insensitive, so keys are lower-cased (e.g. [code]"icy-br"[/code], [code]"content-type"[/code]).

method.name: get_downloaded_bytes
method.description: Returns the amount of bytes downloaded from the beginning of the stream. The counter restarts from [code]0[/code] when a redirect is followed.

method.name: set_audio_decoder
method.description: Sets the decoder that receives the downloaded data, instead of letting the stream create one for each connection from the content type. Call it before [method request]. The same decoder is then used for every connection until it is replaced, and the stream does not set [code]icy-br[/code] on it. Pass [code]null[/code] to let the stream create decoders again. Data is pushed into the decoder directly from the download thread, not through the main thread.

members.member: If no data arrives for this many seconds, the connection is closed with [constant RESULT_TIMEOUT]. The timer restarts with every received chunk. [code]0[/code] disables it. Keep it longer than the decoder's buffer (about 8 seconds at 128 kbps), so a short network problem that the buffer can cover does not close the connection. The value is read when [method request] is called.

constants.constant: The server sent the whole body of a response with a known length. A live stream has no length, so it never ends this way.
A TCP connection to the host could not be established.
The host name could not be resolved.
The connection failed during the TLS handshake, while sending the request or while reading the response.
The response headers did not arrive within the [code]connect_timeout[/code] passed to [method request], or no data arrived for longer than [member stall_timeout].
The server closed the connection before its response headers were complete, or returned a non-2xx status code (HTTP or ICY). Use [method get_response_code] to inspect the status.
The server redirected more times than allowed.

The server closed the connection, which is how a live stream ends. Over HTTPS, a server that closes without a TLS close notice can't be told apart from a broken connection, so that is reported as [constant RESULT_CONNECTION_ERROR].
The request was cancelled with [method cancel_request].
A redirect response was received but could not be followed: the [code]Location[/code] header was missing or malformed, or the connection to the redirect target failed.
No decoder is registered for the [code]Content-Type[/code] of the response (see [method get_content_mime_type]). Not used when a decoder was set with [method set_audio_decoder].
